stateful_filters.detail: eth_newBlockFilter/eth_newFilter/eth_newPendingTransactionFilter return ids but eth_getFilterChanges answers -32602 'filter not found' for most of them: the load balancer is not sticky (probe-filters-cadence-*.txt)

single_connection_consistency.detail: one WebSocket connection pins one backend; HTTPS calls under the same host name do not

flashblocks.mechanism_observed: the pending tag, re-delivered roughly every 320 ms with growing content

same_number_repeats.conclusion: not load-balancer skew: the repeats above were measured inside one connection, and on the flashblocks host a repeated pending number carries a different hash with monotonically growing transaction count and gasUsed, while on the normal host the same number always carries the same hash

reads_on_a_flashblock_hash.eth_getLogs_by_blockHash: error -32001 block not found: hash <pending hash>
reads_on_a_flashblock_hash.eth_getLogs_at_pending_number: [] (empty, although the same pending block reports transactions)
reads_on_a_flashblock_hash.consequence: a flashblock carries no logs, no receipts and no state root access, so it cannot produce a StateUpdate; FlashblockSource can only observe candidate blocks and reconcile them against canonical ones (§27-31, §73)

serial_four_call_loop.detail: 4 serial round-trips take longer than the 1 s cadence, so a live source must walk block numbers rather than only reading the head

polling_ingestion.detection_lag_note: wall clock at read minus block.timestamp, so it contains both the provider's propagation delay and this loop's own serial work

log_source_equivalence.consequence: live ingestion can build the same ChainLog/BlockData the M1 fixtures contain from eth_getBlockReceipts alone, which is what lets Replay and Live share one decode path

safety_note: eth_sendRawTransaction IS whitelisted on this public endpoint (it reached the node and answered -32602 typed transaction too short). M5 must therefore prove by test, not by assertion, that this codebase never calls it (§26, §71).
